Plot the posterior distribution of a network metric

Source: R/metrics.R
plot_metric.Rd

Plots the posterior distribution of a network metric from extract_metric(), which shows the most plausible values of the metric and how uncertain it is. Continuous metrics are shown as smoothed densities; metrics that only take whole-number values (such as degree) are shown as bar charts. A matrix with several columns (for example, one per node) gives one plot per column.

Usage

plot_metric(x, metric_name = "Network Metric", ...)

Arguments

x

A matrix of metric samples from extract_metric().

metric_name

Label for the x axis. With several columns, the column name or number is added to it.

...

Additional arguments passed to the plotting function (graphics::barplot() or graphics::curve()), such as xlim.

Value

NULL, invisibly. The function is called for its plots.

See also

extract_metric()

Examples

sim_data <- simulate_bison_model("binary", aggregated = TRUE)
fit_edge <- bison_model(
  (event | effort) ~ dyad(node_1_id, node_2_id),
  data = sim_data$df_sim,
  model_type = "binary_conjugate",
  priors = get_default_priors("binary_conjugate")
)
plot_metric(extract_metric(fit_edge, "global_cv", num_draws = 200), "CV of edge weights")
